solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Sign dry drink tipped over (6)

indicatorNotes.tipped over: something tipped over ends up the other way round, so the letters read backwards

blocks.note: a sip is a small drink

annotation.surface: Someone knocks over a glass of dry wine.
annotation.walkthrough: SEC is the wine-list word for dry. The sign is a zodiac sign, not a road sign.
annotation.definitionFit: Pisces, the fish, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

entries.clue: I buy and sell just the way I want (5)

blocks.note: to deal is to buy and sell

annotation.surface: A trader boasts of doing business entirely on their own terms.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one sentence; the break falls after 'sell', and 'I' does double duty in the surface as the speaker.
annotation.definitionFit: Something ideal is exactly as you would wish it.

entries.clue: Descend from there, dear Lord! (4,3,2)

blocks.note: literally, get down off the thing you are on

annotation.surface: Someone begs a climber to get down from somewhere dangerous.
annotation.walkthrough: One phrase, two readings: a literal order to climb down, and the idiom that scoffs at a claim.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Come off it!' and 'dear Lord!' are both cries of incredulity; read literally it tells someone to get down.

entries.clue: Son regularly in temper (6)

annotation.surface: A father complains that his boy keeps losing his temper.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Temper' looks like a noun for anger; here it is the verb meaning to moderate.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to temper anger or criticism is to make it milder.

entries.clue: Wet blanket for Arctic swimmer? (4,4)

blocks.note: taken literally, a fish in freezing water

annotation.surface: A spoilsport is likened to a creature from icy seas.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical second reading: a fish living in Arctic water is literally cold.
annotation.definitionFit: A cold fish is an aloof, unemotional person, much like a wet blanket who dampens any fun.

entries.clue: Character scratching head after a ticking off – me, say? (9,6)

indicatorNotes.scratching head: scratching off its head removes the first letter
indicatorNotes.after: the second part comes after the first

blocks.note: a ticking off is an exchange of cross (angry) words
LETTER, a character, without its first letter

annotation.surface: Someone puzzled and scratching their head after being told off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Scratching head' suggests puzzlement, but it strips the L from LETTER. 'Me' is the setter speaking of themself, hence 'say?'.
annotation.definitionFit: The 'me' of the clue is whoever wrote it: a crossword setter.

entries.clue: Machine tool, scarlet, washed (8)

blocks.note: a lathe turns wood or metal

annotation.surface: A list describing a red machine tool that has been cleaned.
annotation.walkthrough: The commas make it read like an inventory; the definition is simply the last word.
annotation.definitionFit: Lathered means covered in soapy foam, as when washed.

entries.clue: Bone in bird between fulmar’s wings (5)

indicatorNotes.between: the bird sits between the two letters
indicatorNotes.wings: wings are at the edges, so the outer letters

blocks.note: the first and last letters of FULMAR
the emu is a flightless bird

annotation.surface: A bone lodged in a seabird's wing.
annotation.walkthrough: A fulmar is a real seabird, which makes 'wings' look anatomical; here it means only the outside letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the thigh's long bone is one example of a bone.

entries.clue: Bitterly sliced through by the wind (9)

indicatorNotes.sliced through by: a blade slicing through something ends up inside it

annotation.surface: A bitter wind that cuts right through you.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bitterly' and 'wind' seem to go together as a cold blast; in fact 'the wind' splits, with THE going into the word.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: air blowing up from the south is one kind of wind.

entries.clue: Frozen ground melted for stream along with pond, initially (10)

indicatorNotes.melted: melting loses the shape, so the letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.initially: 'initially' means at the start, so only the start of the word, its first letter, is used

blocks.note: these nine letters are melted, along with the P, into a new order

annotation.surface: Frozen ground thaws into streams and ponds.
annotation.walkthrough: The irony is that permafrost is ground that never melts.
annotation.definitionFit: Permafrost is ground that stays frozen all year round.

entries.clue: Claw measured, as unusually long, first of all (4)

indicatorNotes.first of all: the first letter of all the words that follow

blocks.note: first letters of Measured As Unusually Long

annotation.surface: A claw is measured and found to be unusually long.
annotation.walkthrough: 'First of all' sounds like 'to begin with' but means the first letter of each word.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain verb synonyms: an animal that claws its prey tears at it savagely.

entries.clue: Dropped bricks in underwear! (8)

blocks.note: to drop a brick is to make a gaffe; a bloomer is a blunder

annotation.surface: Bricks tumble out of someone's knickers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drop a brick' is British slang for making an embarrassing blunder, and a bloomer is the same thing.
annotation.definitionFit: Bloomers are both gaffes and loose women's knickers.

entries.clue: Tray he soiled, dirty (6)

indicatorNotes.soiled: something soiled has been messed up, so the letters are jumbled

annotation.surface: A man has made a mess of a tray.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Soiled' and 'dirty' look like one idea repeated; the first is the instruction, the second the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses match: smelling of soil, and crude or bawdy, the sense of a dirty joke.

entries.clue: Idle brain (4)

blocks.note: a verb here: to laze about doing nothing
rhyming slang for the head, from a word that rhymes with bread

annotation.surface: A lazy mind.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Loaf' for head comes from rhyming slang, loaf of bread = head; 'use your loaf' means think.
annotation.definitionFit: The first is a plain verb synonym for lazing about; the second is rhyming slang, loaf of bread for head, hence the brain.

entries.clue: Remove from power with open question about king (9)

annotation.surface: Rebels plot to depose a monarch by raising an open question about him.
annotation.walkthrough: R for king is from the Latin rex.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: toppling a ruler or government, usually by force.

entries.clue: Cook’s stuff lost on weaver (8)

indicatorNotes.lost: letters that are lost have wandered out of order

annotation.surface: A weaver has mislaid some material.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stuff' suggests cloth next to a weaver; here it means the dishes a cook uses.
annotation.definitionFit: Ovenware is the heatproof dishes a cook uses.

entries.clue: Ferocious beast, furious lover tucked into Chardonnay, say (9)

indicatorNotes.furious: furious means wildly agitated, so the letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.tucked into: one thing is put inside another

blocks.note: Chardonnay is a kind of wine

annotation.surface: An angry lover drowns their sorrows in white wine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks Chardonnay as an example of the category wanted, wine.
annotation.definitionFit: The wolverine is a fierce, powerful animal of the weasel family.

entries.clue: Original butcher ate rice, starter of venison put away (8)

indicatorNotes.butcher: to butcher is to hack apart, so the letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.starter of: a starter is what begins a meal, so the starter of a word is its opening letter
indicatorNotes.put away: put away inside, as food is put away in a stomach

annotation.surface: An inventive butcher sits down to rice and a venison starter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Butcher' looks like a person eating; it is a verb telling you to mangle ATE RICE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: original thinking is inventive and imaginative.

entries.clue: Overhaul due, after getting promoted (8)

indicatorNotes.Overhaul: an overhaul takes something apart and rebuilds it

annotation.surface: Someone is due a shake-up after being promoted.
annotation.walkthrough: 'After' looks like a sequence word, but it is part of the letters to be rearranged.
annotation.definitionFit: Something featured has been given prominence, or promoted.

entries.clue: Places in lounge discussed? (4)

indicatorNotes.discussed?: something discussed is spoken, so we want a sound

annotation.surface: Spots in a lounge that people talk about.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Places' looks like a noun; it is the verb, as in lays a book on the table, and 'lounge' is a verb too.
annotation.definitionFit: To place something is to lay it down.

entries.clue: Pieced together puzzle understood, some steps taken to start it (6)

indicatorNotes.to start it: this piece goes at the front

blocks.note: a jig is a lively dance, a set of steps

annotation.surface: Someone finally grasps a puzzle and takes steps to begin it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pieced together' is part of the definition: a jigsaw is a puzzle you piece together.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: a picture cut into interlocking shapes that the solver reassembles.

entries.clue: Contribution from Gaia, the nature goddess (6)

indicatorNotes.Contribution from: a contribution is a part of the whole, so the answer is part of the words

annotation.surface: Something given by Gaia, the Greek earth goddess.
annotation.walkthrough: Gaia is herself a goddess, which makes her the tempting answer; she only houses it.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the Greek deity of wisdom is one goddess among many.

entries.clue: Classic place bagged by sheep sometimes (5)

indicatorNotes.bagged by: to bag something is to capture it, so the answer is caught inside the letters of the words that follow

annotation.surface: A place that sheep sometimes graze.
annotation.walkthrough: The classics are England's five great flat horse races; two, the Derby and the Oaks, are run at Epsom Downs in Surrey.
annotation.definitionFit: Epsom is the racecourse that hosts two of the classic races.

entries.clue: Contagion, great film, half claimed (8)

indicatorNotes.claimed: what is claimed is taken and held, so it goes inside

blocks.note: an epic is a grand film
demi- is a prefix meaning half

annotation.surface: A review of the film Contagion calls it great, half-heartedly.
annotation.walkthrough: Contagion is also the name of a 2011 pandemic film, which makes 'great film' feel like a review, and 'half claimed' feel like an amount.
annotation.definitionFit: An epidemic is a widespread outbreak of contagious disease.

entries.clue: Asian artist on question one after opening of investigation (5)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down answer, one piece on another sits above it
indicatorNotes.after: this group follows the first letter
indicatorNotes.opening of: the opening of something is where it begins, so the opening of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: An Asian painter questioned when an inquiry begins.
annotation.walkthrough: RA, a member of the Royal Academy, is the usual crossword artist.
annotation.definitionFit: Iraq is in western Asia, so an Iraqi is an Asian.

entries.clue: War god is brave, though no leader (4)

blocks.note: DARES, is brave, without its first letter

annotation.surface: A god of war who fights bravely but without commanding.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Is brave' is a verb phrase, so it gives DARES rather than a word like BOLD.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the Greek deity of battle, Mars to the Romans.

entries.clue: Gut ain’t silent when windy! (10)

annotation.definitionNote: 'Gut' is used as a modifier, as in gut ache, so it matches the adjective

indicatorNotes.when windy: windy as in twisting, so the letters wind about

annotation.surface: A rumbling stomach that won't keep quiet when it has wind.
annotation.walkthrough: Windy suggests flatulence, a joke about the gut; as the instruction it means winding, twisting.
annotation.definitionFit: The noun used as a modifier, as in gut bacteria, carries the adjective's sense of the bowel.

entries.clue: Promise to cover rear in bikini by maiden with – this? (8)

annotation.definition: Promise to cover rear in bikini by maiden with – this?

indicatorNotes.to cover: one thing goes over and around another
indicatorNotes.rear in: the rear of anything is its back end, so the rear in a word is its last letter

blocks.note: M = maiden, a cricket scorebook term

annotation.surface: A pledge that a young woman's bikini will cover her behind.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: swimwear covering a maiden's rear. A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored.
annotation.definitionFit: Read straight, the whole clue asks what a maiden wears to keep her rear covered: the category a bikini belongs to.

entries.clue: Miniature dish, it’s sad to see (6)

annotation.surface: Someone finds a tiny pie a sorry sight.
annotation.walkthrough: A weepie is a tear-jerking film, a sad thing to see.
annotation.definitionFit: A weepie is a sentimental film that makes you cry.
